Today is my legitimate day off!
My only jeans are in the wash right now.
This is a restaurant, not a home laundromat.
And whose little angry dog is this?
This is Tyson, Nagiyev's favorite dog.
Careful, the dog grabbed my hot dog!
Tyson, drop it, drop the sausage immediately!
Oh, it seems the dog was hit by electric current!
My God, he is lying and not breathing!
I told you, this socket is broken!
What will I say to Dmitry Vladimirovich now?
Calm down, let's put the dog in a bag.
Quick, let's run to the vet to save the dog!

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.en: to run (in one direction), to flee, to escape
meanings.note: irregular mixed conjugation: бегу, бежишь, ..., бегут

examples.trans: Run, Marina, before it's too late!
Where are you running so fast?

examples.text: Надо бежать! Беги в деревню к маме.
examples.trans: You need to run! Run to the village to your mum's.

meanings.note: слава богу = thank God (literally 'glory to God')

examples.text: О, наконец тепло! Слава богу. Сейчас ещё чай сделаю.
examples.trans: Oh, it's warm at last! Thank goodness. Now I'll make some tea too.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to throw; to leave (someone)', paired with 'бросать'.

meanings.en: to leave, to walk out on (someone)

examples.text: Меня жена бросила. Два пальца сломаны.
examples.trans: My wife has left me. Two of my fingers are broken.
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'veterinarian, vet' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: They quickly ran to the veterinarian.

examples.text: Быстрее бежим к ветеринару спасать пса!
examples.trans: Quick, let's run to the vet to save the dog!

examples.text: Решается ваш вопрос, Клавдия Викторовна! Вы не видите, у меня встреча?
examples.trans: Your question is being sorted out, Klavdia Viktorovna! Can't you see I have a meeting?

meanings.note: substantivized adjective from выходной день; declines like an adjective

examples.trans: It's a day off, after all.

examples.text: Что ты делаешь в эти выходные?
examples.trans: What are you doing this weekend?
It is the weekend today, everything is cool!

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

meanings.note: Я тебе говорю = I'm telling you
+ infinitive: давай убирать = let's clean up

related.gloss: to give (the verb it comes from)

meanings.note: на днях = in the next few days, or the other day

examples.trans: I'll call in the next few days.
Any day now, on the website.
My jeans are in the wash right now.
My only jeans are in the wash right now.

examples.text: Суд решил: домашний арест по месту прописки.
examples.trans: The court has decided: house arrest at his registered address.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to breathe'.

examples.text: Лёша, что случилось? Дыши, сынок, дыши!
examples.trans: Lyosha, what happened? Breathe, son, breathe!

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('only, sole').

examples.trans: This performance is our only chance!
My only jeans are in the wash right now.

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'конный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('legitimate, lawful').

examples.trans: Today is my legitimate day off.

examples.text: У меня сегодня законный выходной день!
examples.trans: Today is my legitimate day off!

examples.text: Я согласна стать твоей законной женой!
examples.trans: I agree to become your lawful wife!

meanings.note: злая собака = vicious dog; а почему вы такая злая? = why are you so hostile?
emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: мне кажется = I think, it seems to me

examples.trans: I think I've seen you somewhere.

meanings.en: to lie, to be lying down, to rest

examples.text: Такие люди должны лежать в особенном месте!
examples.trans: Such people should lie in a special place!
The book is lying on the table.
But I'll be lying next to Grishka for eternity.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('favourite, beloved').

examples.text: А ты готовишь мой любимый торт со сгущёнкой!
examples.trans: And you make my favourite condensed milk cake!

examples.text: А ты готовишь мой любимый торт со сгущёнкой! До вечера, Марина.
examples.trans: And you make my favourite condensed milk cake! See you tonight, Marina.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('small, little').
goes right before the word it negates
Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'медленно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'plastic bag, carrier bag, packet' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Пакет с ветки снимешь — и отдам.
examples.trans: Take the bag off the branch and I'll give it to you.
Do you need a carrier bag?

meanings.en: to put, to place, to lay down

examples.text: В гроб с собой икру не положишь!
examples.trans: You can't put caviar in your coffin to take with you!
Put the keys on the table.

examples.text: А вот сюда я её и положу! Отличный подарок будет!
examples.trans: Right here is where I will put it! It will be an excellent gift!
Why are we going so slowly?

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!
This is a restaurant, not a laundromat.

examples.text: Здесь ресторан, а не домашняя прачечная.
examples.trans: This is a restaurant, not a home laundromat.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'dog, hound' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: To give boots to vicious dogs.

examples.text: Сначала мы отдадим твои сапоги злым псам.
examples.trans: First we will give your boots to the vicious dogs.

examples.text: Слушай, Нина, это же тот самый ресторан!
examples.trans: Listen, Nina, this is that very restaurant!

examples.text: Мы рады видеть вас в нашем ресторане.
examples.trans: We are glad to see you in our restaurant.
They called from the Italian restaurant.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'socket, electrical outlet' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This socket on the wall is broken.

examples.text: Я же говорил, эта розетка сломана!
examples.trans: I told you, this socket is broken!

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: сломать руку = to break one's arm

examples.text: Меня жена бросила. Два пальца сломаны.
examples.trans: My wife has left me. Two of my fingers are broken.

meanings.note: grammatically feminine even for a male dog

examples.text: А с другой стороны, ты ешь обычные сосиски.
examples.trans: And on the other hand, you eat ordinary sausages.

meanings.en: to save, to rescue from danger
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to save, to rescue', paired with 'спасти'.

examples.text: Все прибежали тебя спасать — и я, и папа!
examples.trans: Everyone came running to save you — both me and Dad!
She is saving you from the hospital!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'покойно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Его не будет часа два. Вы спокойно всё сделаете.
examples.trans: He'll be gone for about two hours. You'll do everything calmly.

meanings.en: to do the washing, to wash clothes
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тирать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to wash (clothes)', paired with 'постирать'.

examples.text: Я уже не могу готовить, стирать, убирать. Я хочу на море!
examples.trans: I can't take the cooking, washing and cleaning any more. I want to go to the sea!

meanings.en: to grab, to seize, to snatch
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'хватить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to grab, to snatch', paired with 'хватать'.

examples.text: Схватил собачку в парке и побежал.
examples.trans: Grab the little dog in the park and run.
He grabbed the bag off the table.

examples.text: Да это легко. Схватил собачку в парке и побежал.
examples.trans: Come on, it's easy. Grab the little dog in the park and run.

examples.text: Теперь я начальник нашей стройки. Ты уволен!
examples.trans: Now I'm the boss of our building site. You're fired!

meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'electric current' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The dog was hit by an electric current.
Oh, it seems the dog was hit by electric current!

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.en: to hit, to strike, to punch
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'дарить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to hit, to strike', paired with 'ударять'.

examples.trans: He struck the table with his fist.

examples.text: Вот если бы он ребёнка ударил!
examples.trans: Now if he had hit a child!

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'uniform, form, shape' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The cook put on a clean uniform.

examples.text: Шеф, мне не выдали форму вовремя.
examples.trans: Chef, they did not issue my uniform on time.
All employees wear a clean uniform.

фу.gloss: drop it! (to a dog); ugh, yuck

examples.text: Лютик, Лютик! Фу! Что ты там делаешь? Лютик, стой!
examples.trans: Lyutik, Lyutik! Drop it! What are you doing there? Lyutik, stop!

ходить.gloss: to walk, to go (on foot, regularly)

meanings.en: to walk, to go on foot
meanings.note: back and forth or habitually; one trip in one direction: идти

examples.text: Мальчик ходит на костылях. А она ещё и активистка.
examples.trans: The boy walks on crutches. And she's an activist, too.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'hot dog' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The dog grabbed my hot dog.
Careful, the dog grabbed my hot dog!

meanings.note: agrees with the thing owned: чей дом, чья машина, чьё письмо, чьи деньги

examples.text: Курица? Нет. А чей это холодильник?
examples.trans: Chicken? No. And whose fridge is this?

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
